For me it's the original sonic adventure. Because oh man does that game have flaws

It's glitchy, it's ugly, it's cut-scene animations are the worst I've ever seen, only two of the playable characters are plot relevant, one is a boring slow paced platformer, and another one is entirely mandatory fishing (big and amy)

But the game's controls (at least for sonic tails, knuckles and maybe gamma) are fucking perfect, the level design is open and fantastic, and the soundtrack is my favorite in the franchise (and that's saying something)
(Discussion) What is the most flawed or poorly aged game that you love

Age of Empires I. Unit cap of 50 unless you play Multiplayer (if I recall correctly), siege weapons are hilariously imbalanced when used en mass, you constantly need to manually babysit your farms, no multi-unit production unless you own the XPAC, keeping units with different speed in formation is a pain in the ass, and the scenario editor is extremely limited when it comes to triggers and such.

And I still get an almost obscene amount of nostalgia when I boot up the game and the first villager greets me with a friendly "Rogan?"
I bet some of the older folks would choose Adventure. That thing would never get greenlit on Steam by people who don't know its origins.
Most likely the original Syphon Filter trilogy. I'm still baffled that the control scheme used in them wasn't picked back up for the PSP releases.

The original pokemon games have a certain charm to them. The one I love best, though, is always going to be Pokemon Yellow - having that pikachu follow you around everywhere was just so unbearably cute.
As antiquated as the gameboy graphics are, Pokemon still has a huge following

Legacy of Kain: Soul Reaver

Sooo clippy in places. But the voices, the story, the game play - it was a first of awesomes for me and I love it so much.

Persona 2 Innocent Sin for me. Flawed combat, poorly thought out dungeons, badly translated, and a learning curve so steep it is a learning cliff. But it showed me a different kind of RPG, and I love it for that.
Have you played the PSP remastering? It's good.
I have not, since it is on PSP it should be fairly cheap used. I will try to find a copy today.

Skyrim. One of the most broken games I've ever played, in almost every aspect. No challenge, no story worth mentioning, just a massive, exploitable grindfest which ultimately has no purpose. It remains however the most relaxing game I've ever played, with its (still) astonishing visuals and soothing music, it just oozes with atmosphere. I can get over all the bugginess and lack of purpose cause they don't get in the way of the immersion. A terrible RPG, a wonderful walking simulator.

Not flawed or poorly aged in the usual sense, but my fond memories of Day of the Tentacle, Full Throttle, and Grim Fandango are now tainted by the recent revelations about Tim Schafer's politics. He used to be cool...
Gish. It has a lot of potential being a platformer that takes a long time to master but nowdays the you can't consistently move from one place to other, physics are somewhat buggy and so on.

Azure Dreams maybe? People seem pretty mixed toward that game, but it was a beautiful little rogue-like, monster-taming game with some dating sim elements peppered in, great artwork imo, interesting town upgrade system, charming quests and characters , difficult gameplay, and great music. I come back to this game occasionally every few years and am never disappointed.

Btw, im talking about the psx version, not the gba version.

Final Fantasy VII has not aged well in the slightest. I look fondly back on it as one of my favorite games ever, and I was kind of stunned when I saw people were actually silly enough to go out and pay $15 for a half-baked port on PS4.

I own the ps1 discs and the PC version and it's a hot mess. At the time it was entirely cutting edge with its cut scenes and the gameplay was par for the course. The material system I still don't care for over the first six games magic systems though. Now though the game is horrendous to look at and a mediocre game to play at best.

R4: Ridge Racer Type 4 for me. In terms of style, aesthetic, soundtrack, weaving a story into a racing game, etc, I really don't think it has ever been topped. But the driving itself has aged very poorly. What I wouldn't do for a modern update of that game. Sometimes I fantasize about an Atlus-Namco team up to make a follow up. Compared side by side, it's really interesting to see how much of style crossover there is between Persona and R4.

Gex: Deep Cover Gecko. It's buried in my mind that it had an awesome camera control system, with amazing graphics. But the reality is, the camera is terrible and the graphics have not aged very well compared to most other games from the era.

I still love it though. The humour and level design makes up for it.
